messages:
olivia: Ran a 60s perfetto capture for the full e2e (client->gateway->runtime) during a small qps ramp. KV cache starts doing full-scans around 00:01:23 which lines up with tail latency spikes. Trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/0a1b2c3d :eyes:

sanjay: Nice. Which categories did you enable? I want kernel+kv+sched so we can correlate locks and disk IO.

olivia: Ran with:
```
--categories=cpu,kernel,track_event,disabled_unwinder
--buffer-size-mb=512
--duration=60
```
Also captured NVTX from gateway/runtime.

kevin: Looking at the flame, runtime.kv_fetch spans are often followed by a ~30-80ms kernel_select gap. That gap is the tail.

marie: Did you correlate with batching? Our heuristic toggles around 8->12 tokens and has a small hysteresis.

olivia: Yes. When the batch threshold flips we temporarily reshuffle kernel profiles and KV prefetch misses spike. Example span order from the flame:
```
client.request -> gateway.enqueue -> gateway.proxy_send -> runtime.scheduler -> runtime.kv_fetch -> runtime.kernel_select -> runtime.execute
```
Gaps are between kv_fetch and kernel_select.

sanjay: Could kv_fetch be blocking on NVMe reads? Which environment?

olivia: Dedicated cluster (ded-2a), quantized shards on NVMe. I also ran an nsys kernel timeline; NVTX shows stalls pinned to thread 7.

kevin: Can you paste the event slice around 00:01:23?

olivia: Slice:
```
00:01:22.980 client.request start
00:01:22.985 gateway.proxy_send start
00:01:23.010 runtime.kv_fetch start
00:01:23.070 runtime.kv_fetch end
00:01:23.071 runtime.kernel_select start
00:01:23.150 runtime.kernel_select end
00:01:23.151 runtime.execute start
```
kv_fetch ~90ms, kernel_select ~80ms in this capture.

marie: 90ms is too high for kv_fetch. Could be GC or queue backpressure.

kevin: Also check kernel_selector lock contention. We recently added a global lock to dedupe compiles.

olivia: Instrumented with `tracepoint(kernel_selector,fingerprint)` and I see multiple threads blocked on `kernel_registry_lock` at the same time as the spike.

sanjay: That's from my change yesterday — I added a global compile lock to avoid duplicate kernels. Looks like it regressed under bursty load.

kevin: Short-term fix: per-model mutex or double-checked locking so the critical section is tiny. Longer-term add compile-state machine.

marie: Also mitigate by increasing batching hysteresis so thresholds don't flip on transient bursts (e.g., require 3 consecutive batches to cross threshold).

olivia: I'll patch runtime/kernel_selector.cc to use per-model locks and rerun perfetto on staging.

deploy-bot: deploy started by olivia on staging at 2025-07-12T15:42:10Z :rocket:

olivia: Patch deployed to staging, ran same workload and capture (new trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/updated123) :white_check_mark:

kevin: Quick look — kernel_select is now ~5-12ms, kv_fetch stabilized ~20ms. Lock contention appears resolved.

sanjay: Opening PR to revert the global-lock change and add concurrent-selection tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3456

marie: I'll add a regression test that simulates batch-threshold flapping.

olivia: Attaching perfetto+nsys artifacts to the PR and running canary.

perfetto-bot: Perfetto trace uploaded by olivia (18MB). View: https://perfetto.dev/trace/updated123

kevin: Action items: sanjay - PR, marie - hysteresis test, olivia - perf artifacts + canary capture.

olivia: Running final canary capture now, will post results in #eng-runtime.

kevin: :thumbsup:

marie: :100:
